swarm.title: Swarm
swarm.blurb: This drone's place in the fleet, the formation it defaults to, and the flocking and separation envelopes it flies inside.
swarm.slotHint: Issued by the ground station at pair time. Formation offsets are indexed by it, so it is reported here and edited nowhere.
swarm.enabledHint: Master switch for the node's swarm services.
swarm.formationHint: The formation preset the node starts with. Only these five exist; anything else produces no formation at all.
swarm.spacingHint: Inter-drone spacing for formations, in meters.
swarm.cohesionHint: Pull toward the local group's centre, as a percentage of unit gain (40 means 0.40).
swarm.alignmentHint: Match the local group's heading and speed, as a percentage of unit gain (60 means 0.60).
swarm.separationGainHint: Strength of the push away from a close neighbour, as a percentage of unit gain (150 means 1.50).
swarm.flockRadiusHint: Neighbours beyond this range contribute nothing to cohesion or alignment.
swarm.flockNeighborsHint: How many of the nearest neighbours inside the radius are weighted, so a dense cluster cannot dominate the solution.
swarm.sepRadiusHint: Below this distance the drone pushes away from a neighbour. Must stay above the hard floor.
swarm.sepHardHint: Below this distance the horizontal solution is abandoned for a hold and a slot-indexed climb, overriding every other mode.
swarm.separationConfirmMessage: Separation is the collision-avoidance layer, not a preference. A larger value makes the fleet spread; a smaller one lets aircraft close on each other before anything intervenes. Apply this change?
swarm.precedenceHint: Highest authority first. A drone whose separation layer has taken over is in hard separation whatever mode was commanded.
swarm.precedenceHardSeparation: Hard separation — a neighbour inside the hard floor
swarm.runtimeNotice: These values drive the node's onboard swarm runtime, which picks up a saved change within a few seconds. It commands the flight controller only while Enabled is on and the aircraft reports GUIDED, so saving here does not by itself put the node under swarm control.

macPin.title: MAC pinning
macPin.blurb: An adapter without a hardware MAC randomizes its address each boot, which churns the node's DHCP lease and IP. The agent pins a stable MAC so the address stops moving.
macPin.enabledHint: Pin a stable MAC on adapters that report no hardware address. The pin is written as a next-boot rule and never touches the live link.
macPin.applyLiveHint: Also allow re-tagging the live interface so the address changes without a reboot. This drops any connection riding that interface, and is always refused on the management interface.
macPin.notReported: This node has not reported adapter stability.
macPin.noneTracked: The agent reports no adapters that need MAC pinning.
macPin.candidateHint: This adapter looks like it randomizes its MAC. Confirm the pin on the node with
macPin.dhcpHint: Add a DHCP reservation for a pinned MAC to fix the node's IP as well.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.blurb: How this node announces itself on the LAN, and the reach names and URLs it advertises.
discovery.mdnsHint: Publish this node on the LAN so it can be found by name. Takes effect when the agent restarts.
discovery.advertisedHint: Names and URLs come verbatim from the node's own report — nothing here is constructed by the app.
discovery.requiresLan: The advertised reach names can only be read over the node's LAN connection.
discovery.loadFailed: Could not read the node's advertised names.
discovery.urlsEmpty: The node reports no reachable URLs.

selfHeal.title: Self-heal
selfHeal.blurb: Always-on protections that repair the node's own connectivity and camera without operator action.
selfHeal.wifiSelfHealHint: Re-associates the onboard management Wi-Fi when it is connected but passing no traffic. Only ever touches onboard managed Wi-Fi, never the radio adapter or a wired link.
selfHeal.cameraRecoveryHint: Recovers an expected camera that failed to enumerate by re-binding the device or power-cycling its port. Steps that could disturb other devices stay gated.
selfHeal.guardianHint: Watches the operator's path to the node and climbs an escalating repair ladder when the link dies. Always on; tunable only in the node's configuration file.
selfHeal.reconcilerHint: Holds the global regulatory domain to the configured value so a radio adapter's baked-in country can never kill the onboard network. Recent re-pins appear in the activity feed.
selfHeal.eventsUnavailable: Event history needs the node's on-device log store, reachable over the LAN.

mavlinkRouting.title: MAVLink
mavlinkRouting.blurb: How this node connects to the flight controller, exposes MAVLink endpoints, and forwards telemetry.
mavlinkRouting.transportHint: Managed from the node's Overview tab (FC connection picker), which validates the change against a live heartbeat.
mavlinkRouting.endpointsNotReported: The node's configuration does not carry an endpoint list.
mavlinkRouting.systemIdHint: The MAVLink system ID this node's router speaks with (1-255).
mavlinkRouting.componentIdHint: The MAVLink component ID this node's router speaks with (2-255). 1 is the autopilot's own ID and 0 is broadcast, so neither is accepted.
mavlinkRouting.signingRequiresLan: Signing status needs a LAN connection to the node.

security.title: Security
security.blurb: The node's access posture: pairing key state, connection enforcement, and the dashboard PIN.
security.apiKeyHint: Issued when the node is paired; the value is never shown here. To issue a new key, unpair the node and pair it again — in-place rotation is not exposed by the agent.
security.wsEnforceHint: When on, a paired node rejects off-box raw-MAVLink WebSocket connections that present no valid pairing key. On-box and unpaired connections stay open. When off, an unauthorized connection is logged but still admitted.
security.setupTokenHint: When on, every setup mutation needs the token generated on the node at first boot. When off, any browser served the setup pages from the node's own port is trusted.
security.pinHint: Gates the node's own web dashboard when opened from another device. Set or reset it from this node's Health tab, on the Dashboard access card.
security.pinNoPath: The PIN posture can only be read through a stored pairing record for this node. Manage the PIN on the node's own dashboard, or from the Health tab once the node is paired over the LAN.
security.missionControlUrlHint: The Mission Control address this node advertises in its setup flow. Blank offers only a localhost link.
security.restBindHint: The address and port the node's HTTP API listens on. Set at install; changing it needs a reinstall.
security.wsEnforceConfirmMessage: With enforcement off, a paired node admits off-box raw-MAVLink WebSocket connections that present no pairing key, so an unauthenticated caller on the network could send commands straight to the flight controller. Only turn this off on a trusted, isolated link.
security.setupTokenConfirmMessage: With the token no longer required, any browser that can reach the node's setup pages is trusted to change its configuration. Only turn this off on a trusted network.

radio.title: Radio
radio.blurb: Fleet addressing, the WFB link switches and the modulation rung for this node's radio.
radio.notAdvertised: This agent's config surface does not expose a WFB radio block, so there is nothing to configure here.
radio.fleetIdHint: Every node that must hear every other node shares this. Two fleets can share one channel without hearing each other.
radio.fleetSlotHint: Issued by the ground station when this node pairs. Two nodes on one slot re-initialise each other's decoder about once a second, which reads as unexplained link loss — so the slot is never hand-edited here.
radio.presetHint: The MCS + FEC combination the radio starts with. Conservative keeps any explicitly set per-key values.
radio.bandHint: The channel whitelist automatic hopping scans.
radio.autoHopHint: Moves the link to the quietest channel in the band, coordinated with the radio peer.
radio.adaptiveHint: Steps bitrate and FEC down as the link degrades and back up as it recovers.
radio.mcsHint: The modulation rung the transmitter starts on. Each step up buys throughput and costs link margin.
radio.mcsLiveHint: Measured off-air from the peer's frames — the rung actually being transmitted, not the value stored above.
radio.mcsAutoHint: The adaptive ladder owns the rung while adaptive bitrate is on. Turn adaptive off to set one by hand.
radio.mcsCapHint: The highest rung the ladder may climb to. Defaults to 3; anything above it is bench-only until the driver sweep says the rung holds at range. A ceiling of 1 pins the ladder to the floor.
radio.channelHint: The rendezvous channel. Pairing and automatic hopping manage it.
radio.txPowerHint: Managed live from the Link tab's power slider.
radio.fleetIdConfirmMessage: A node hears only nodes with the same fleet ID. After its next radio start this node cannot hear any peer on a different fleet ID, including its ground station, so every node in the fleet must be changed to match.
radio.mcsPresetHint: The link preset sets the rung at every radio start and replaces a stored value. Switch the preset to Conservative to set the rung by hand.

display.title: Display
display.rendererBlurb: Which renderer this ground station brings up at boot. The display service gates its startup on this, and the on-box display is how you recover a node whose network is down, so only renderers the node reports as attached can be selected.
display.kioskBlurb: The full-screen browser the HDMI output runs. Applies when the renderer resolves to HDMI.
display.kioskTargetUrlHint: The page the kiosk opens. Leave empty to use this node's own console.
display.kioskAlwaysOn: The kiosk runs whenever the renderer above resolves to HDMI and a display is attached. To take it off the screen, choose a different renderer.

battery.title: Battery setup
battery.blurb: The limits the node's battery engine checks every flight-controller battery report against. A crossing raises an anomaly on the Live view, in the node's event log, and as an alert here.
battery.orderNote: Critical cell must stay below Low cell. The node rejects a pair that crosses and keeps the previous values.
battery.enabledHint: Evaluate the cell, sag, temperature and time-to-reserve rules on the node. The flight controller's own battery failsafes are not affected either way.
battery.lowCellMvHint: A cell below this raises a warning. 2500 to 4200 mV, above Critical cell.
battery.criticalCellMvHint: A cell below this raises a critical alert. 2500 to 4000 mV, below Low cell.
battery.cellDivergenceMvHint: Spread between the highest and lowest cell that raises a warning. 10 to 500 mV.
battery.voltageDropMvPerSHint: Pack voltage falling faster than this raises a warning. 100 to 5000 mV per second.
battery.tempSpikeDcPerSHint: Pack temperature rising faster than this raises a warning, in tenths of a degree per second (50 is 5 °C/s). 5 to 200.
battery.predictiveWindowSHint: How much recent discharge history the time-to-reserve estimate uses. 5 to 300 seconds.
battery.reservePercentHint: The charge the time-to-reserve estimate counts down to. 5 to 50 percent.

limited.title: Cloud relay connection
limited.network: Network configuration writes through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. Connect to the agent's setup page from a device on the same network to change WiFi, Ethernet, modem, or uplink priority.
limited.display: LCD calibration and remote page control write through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. Read-only status is in the Overview card.
limited.physicalUi: OLED brightness, screen cycle, and Bluetooth pairing route through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. Connect on LAN to make changes.
limited.peripherals: Peripheral rescan and per-peripheral actions route through the agent's REST surface, which is only reachable on the same LAN. The list below comes from the cloud heartbeat and is read-only.
limited.mesh: batman-adv mesh topology (neighbours, routes, gateways) is local to the ground station and never relayed through the cloud. Connect on LAN to inspect mesh health.
limited.distributedRx: Distributed receive fragment counters and pairing controls are local to the ground station and never relayed through the cloud. Connect on LAN for the live view.
limited.radio: Radio link stats and TX power route through this ground station's own REST surface, which is only reachable over a direct connection to it. Connect to this node on the LAN to view or change its radio.
limited.gnss: The GNSS lane and RTK base are read and set through this ground station's own REST surface, which is only reachable over a direct connection to it. Connect to this node on the LAN to view or change them.
limited.lora: The LoRa lane, its duty governor and region are read and set through this ground station's own REST surface, which is only reachable over a direct connection to it. Connect to this node on the LAN to view or change them.
limited.sensors: Rig sensors, the session clock and capture storage are read straight from the node. Open this node on its local network to see them.

videoLatencyBreakdown.droneSideStampToReadback: Drone-side stamp-to-readback: the time between the encoder emitting a frame (where the SEI timestamp is injected, after encode) and that frame being read back off the drone's own RTSP feed. Covers the publish mux, the RTSP publish and the drone-side buffering. It EXCLUDES camera capture, encode, the radio link, the ground ingest and the browser — it is not a glass-to-glass figure.
videoLatencyBreakdown.numberOfSEISamplesRead: Number of SEI samples read by the drone's local tap in the last second. Roughly equal to the encode framerate when SEI is healthy.
videoLatencyBreakdown.webrtcICECandidatePairCurrentRoundTripTi: WebRTC ICE candidate-pair currentRoundTripTime. Same number Chrome shows in chrome://webrtc-internals.
videoLatencyBreakdown.inboundRtpJitterVarianceIn: inbound-rtp.jitter. Variance in packet arrival timing — high values mean the network is delivering frames at uneven cadence.
videoLatencyBreakdown.chromeSDecoderJitterBuffer: Chrome's decoder jitter buffer: how long each frame waits between arriving and being decoded. Grows when the network is jittery; shrinks when the link is smooth.
videoLatencyBreakdown.cumulativeRTPPacketsTheReceiver: Cumulative RTP packets the receiver detected as lost. Climbing values mean either link quality or FEC budget is insufficient.
videoLatencyBreakdown.totalVideoFramesChromeHas: Total video frames Chrome has decoded since this session started.
videoLatencyBreakdown.framesChromeDecodedButCouldn: Frames Chrome decoded but couldn't render in time (compositor pressure, tab in the background).
videoLatencyBreakdown.estimatedDroneBrowserWallClock: Estimated drone↔browser wall-clock offset, derived from /api/time round-trips (Cristian's algorithm). Positive means the drone clock is ahead.

latency-breakdown-parts.encodePlusNetworkFromRVFC: Encode plus network, from rVFC captureTime to receiveTime. captureTime for a remote source is the user agent's estimate from RTCP sender reports plus clock synchronisation, so it is real but only as good as that sync — and unusable for the first second of a session. Reference for a healthy LAN with a hardware-encoded publisher: about 180 ms P50 / 240 ms P95 end to end. That is a reference, not a measurement of this link.
latency-breakdown-parts.jitterBufferPlusDecodePlus: Jitter buffer plus decode plus composite. Both endpoints are timestamps the user agent reports directly on the performance.now() clock.
latency-breakdown-parts.rvfcProcessingDurationTheSummedDecode: rVFC processingDuration: the summed decode time for the frame, reported by the decoder.
latency-breakdown-parts.receiveToPresentMinusDecode: Receive-to-present minus decode. A subtraction of the two rows above, not an observation — nothing reports this hop directly.
latency-breakdown-parts.theVSyncTaxFrom: The v-sync tax, from presentationTime to expectedDisplayTime. expectedDisplayTime is the user agent's PREDICTION of when the frame becomes visible, not a report that it did.
latency-breakdown-parts.captureToPresentedFrameAnchored: Capture to presented frame. Anchored on captureTime, so it carries the same RTCP-synchronisation caveat as the first hop. This is the honest end-to-end figure the receive path achieves; it is not the same quantity as round-trip time, which contains no capture or encode leg at all.
latency-breakdown-parts.whatTheControlLoopCurrently: What the control loop currently asks the receiver's jitter buffer for, chosen from measured freezes, RTP jitter and loss with a 2 s minimum dwell. It replaced a hardcoded 50 ms that no measurement produced. Zero means either the loop found no reason to add buffer, or this browser implements neither receiver knob — with frames arriving and a non-trivial buffer+composite hop above, it is the browser's own depth and nothing here set it.

mcp.title: Control your drones from your AI assistant
mcp.subtitle: ADOS MCP lets Claude Code and other AI clients read and operate your drones through a scoped, audited connection you run on your own machine — directly over your LAN, or through the cloud when you are away.
mcp.readBody: Live status, telemetry, health, and configuration, with the meaning of every field.
mcp.operateBody: Restart services, manage extensions, and adjust configuration on the node.
mcp.safeBody: A scope on every connection, a confirmation on sensitive actions, and an audit on every call.
mcp.connectBody: Run the server on your own machine and point it at Mission Control, then paste the machine credential you generate here:
mcp.credentialNote: The credential is scoped and revocable, and stored only as a hash. Revoke it any time to cut a server off instantly.
mcp.signInToGenerate: Sign in to Mission Control to generate a credential.
